title: Avatar Optics Lab: Light & Lens Simulation
description: The user operates a virtual optics laboratory where a readyplayer.me avatar wears the Khronos sunglasses. The user adjusts lens tint color (RGB channels independently), UV protection level, polarization angle, ambient light intensity, and light source direction to simulate how different optical configurations affect the avatar's visible appearance and a projected light spectrum readout. Conservation of transmitted light energy must hold: increasing absorption in one channel redistributes energy. Full undo/redo history tracks every parameter change.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net). Load readyplayer.me.glb as a humanoid avatar centered at origin and SunglassesKhronos.glb positioned on the avatar's head (find the Head bone or approximate eye-level). Use OrbitControls for camera, starting at front-facing 3/4 view distance ~2m, looking at head height. Add a warm-toned DirectionalLight and soft AmbientLight plus an HDR-less environment approximation using hemisphere light.

Build an HTML/CSS overlay control panel (right side, dark themed) with these coupled inputs: (1) Red tint slider 0-100%, (2) Green tint slider 0-100%, (3) Blue tint slider 0-100%, (4) UV protection slider 0-100%, (5) Polarization angle dial 0-180°, (6) Ambient light intensity slider 0.1-2.0, (7) Light source azimuth angle 0-360°, (8) Light source elevation -45° to 90°. Enforce a conservation law: total RGB absorption R+G+B must equal a constant budget of 150%. If the user raises one channel past the budget, proportionally reduce the others and update their sliders. Display a real-time 'Transmitted Spectrum' bar chart (three colored bars for RGB) below the panel showing how much light passes through the lenses.

Apply lens parameters to the sunglasses material: set the lens meshes (identify by material name or child index) to a MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission, color derived from inverted tint values, ior 1.5, and thickness modulated by UV protection. Rotate a polarization filter overlay (a subtle striped transparent plane parented to the glasses) by the polarization angle. Update the DirectionalLight position from azimuth/elevation spherically.

Implement undo/redo: store each parameter-change snapshot in a history stack. Bind Ctrl+Z for undo and Ctrl+Y for redo, restoring all 8 parameters and updating both UI sliders and 3D scene. Show undo/redo buttons in the panel with step count. Add a 'Reset All' button returning defaults. Animate the avatar with a subtle idle breathing motion (sinusoidal Y-scale on spine). The spectrum bar chart should animate smoothly on changes. Total interaction steps to fully explore: adjust 3 RGB sliders observing conservation (3), change UV and polarization (2), move light source azimuth and elevation (2), adjust ambient (1), undo twice and redo once (3) = 14 steps.
